description: Candlestick Chart View: Add alternative price chart visualization using candlestick patterns. Toggle between line chart and candlestick view. Builds on existing chart infrastructure with minimal disruption to working code.
principles: Rock-solid quality over speed - every feature must be bulletproof before moving on
Comprehensive test coverage - unit tests, integration tests, edge cases
All tests must pass before a story is marked complete
ZERO disruption to existing line chart - candlestick is additive, not replacing
Stability first - if in doubt, keep it simple
Leverage existing OHLC data already in HistoricalData/ChartContext

CRITICAL_RENDERING_NOTES.warning: READ THIS BEFORE ANY WIDGET/RENDERING WORK
CRITICAL_RENDERING_NOTES.textual_colors: Textual uses Rich markup, NOT ANSI escape codes!
CRITICAL_RENDERING_NOTES.unicode_approach: Use box-drawing characters for candle bodies, vertical lines for wicks
CRITICAL_RENDERING_NOTES.existing_patterns: Follow ChartStyle enum pattern - add CANDLESTICK alongside BRAILLE and BLOCK

candlestickOverview.description: Candlestick charts show OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) data in a visual format

components.body: Rectangle between open and close prices
components.upperWick: Line from body top to high price
components.lowerWick: Line from body bottom to low price
components.bullish: Close > Open - typically green/white, shows buying pressure
components.bearish: Close < Open - typically red/black, shows selling pressure

advantages: Shows price range (high-low) not visible in line charts
Standard format traders are familiar with

existingInfrastructure.chartRenderer: viper/widgets/chart_renderer.py - already has ChartStyle enum with BRAILLE/BLOCK
existingInfrastructure.chartContext: viper/widgets/chart_context.py - already carries opens, closes, highs, lows
existingInfrastructure.chartPanel: viper/widgets/chart_panel.py - UI widget that uses ChartRenderer
existingInfrastructure.historyData: viper/services/history_data.py - HistoricalData dataclass has all OHLC fields

dataAvailability.noNewApiCalls: All OHLC data already fetched by existing history service
dataAvailability.noNewDependencies: Pure rendering change using existing data

characterWidth.rationale: Maximizes data density while still showing OHLC structure
characterWidth.alternative_considered: 3-char candles (body + 2 wicks) - rejected for space efficiency
characterWidth.implementation: Use block characters vertically positioned to show body, dots/lines for wicks

unicodeCharacters.bodyChars: Use block characters (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█) for body fill
unicodeCharacters.wickChars: Use vertical line (│) or light vertical (╎) for wicks
unicodeCharacters.combinedApproach: May combine box-drawing with blocks for best visual effect

toggleMechanism.keybinding: 'v' key to cycle chart view: line -> candlestick -> line
toggleMechanism.alternative: Could use 't v' (technical -> view) but single key is simpler for common action

indicatorCompatibility.overlays: SMA/EMA overlays should work on candlestick view
indicatorCompatibility.subPanels: RSI/MACD panels remain unchanged below chart

Verify existing BRAILLE and BLOCK styles still work unchanged
100% test coverage on style dispatch logic
Test: new enum value exists and is usable
Test: existing styles produce identical output as before
userStories.notes: Foundation change. Stub implementation allows incremental development. Must not break existing charts.

userStories.title: Implement candlestick rendering logic
acceptanceCriteria: Implement _render_candlestick() method in ChartRenderer
Each candle represents one data point (open, high, low, close)
Candle body shows open-to-close range using block characters
Upper wick extends from body top to high
Lower wick extends from body bottom to low
Bullish candles (close > open) colored green
Bearish candles (close < open) colored red
Doji candles (close == open) shown as horizontal line
Y-axis scaling uses full high-low range (not just closes)
Downsampling preserves OHLC structure (use representative candle, not average)
Handle edge case: all candles same price (flat line)
100% test coverage on candlestick rendering
Test: bullish candle renders correctly
Test: bearish candle renders correctly
Test: doji candle renders correctly
Test: wicks extend to high/low correctly
userStories.notes: Core rendering logic. Focus on clarity over density - better to show fewer candles clearly than many candles poorly.

userStories.title: Add chart style toggle keybinding with interval display
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'v' keybinding to ChartPanel: toggle chart view style
Cycle through styles: BRAILLE -> CANDLESTICK -> BRAILLE (skip BLOCK for simplicity)
Store _chart_style: ChartStyle = ChartStyle.BRAILLE in ChartPanel
Re-render chart immediately on style change (no refetch needed)
Show current style AND interval in chart header when candlestick mode active
Header format: 'AAPL - 1M Chart [Candlestick · Daily]' or similar
Map interval codes to human-readable: 1d->Daily, 1wk->Weekly, 1mo->Monthly
Interval indicator helps users understand what each candle represents
Update help_screen.py with 'v' keybinding documentation
Keybinding only active when ChartPanel has focus
100% test coverage on toggle logic
Test: 'v' cycles through styles correctly
Test: chart re-renders on style change
Test: header shows correct interval for each period
userStories.notes: Simple toggle - data already loaded, just re-render with different style. No network calls needed. Interval display is especially useful for candlesticks so users know if they're looking at daily, weekly, or monthly candles.

candlestickRendering.approach: Single character per candle for maximum data density
candlestickRendering.bodyRepresentation: Use vertical position + block height to show body
candlestickRendering.wickRepresentation: Use braille dots or thin line characters above/below body

downsamplingStrategy.problem: More data points than screen width
downsamplingStrategy.solution: Group periods and create representative OHLC candle
downsamplingStrategy.note: This preserves price range information lost in simple averaging

yAxisScaling.lineChart: Currently uses close prices for min/max
yAxisScaling.candlestickChart: Must use high/low for min/max to show full wicks
yAxisScaling.implementation: Pass scaling_mode parameter or auto-detect from chart style

unicodeOptions.brailleDots: Can combine braille patterns for wick rendering
unicodeOptions.recommendation: Start simple with blocks, iterate on visual quality

testingStrategy: Unit tests: candlestick rendering with known OHLC values
Unit tests: downsampling preserves OHLC structure
Visual tests: manual verification of chart appearance
Regression tests: existing line chart unchanged
